rejected.title: Proton NMR spectroscopy
card: Proton NMR looks at the hydrogen atoms in a molecule. Hydrogen atoms in the same surroundings are one environment and give one peak, so the number of peaks is the number of hydrogen environments.
The area under a peak (shown by the integration trace) is proportional to the number of hydrogen atoms in that environment. A peak with twice the area comes from twice as many hydrogens.

The chemical shift of a peak, in ppm, shows what the hydrogens are bonded near. For example, hydrogens next to an electronegative atom or a C=O group appear at a different shift from those in a plain alkyl group.
Splitting shows neighbours. A peak splits into n + 1 lines, where n is the number of hydrogens on the adjacent carbon atoms. Two neighbouring hydrogens give a triplet.
rejected.remember: Peaks count environments, area counts hydrogens, shift shows surroundings, and splitting (n + 1) shows neighbours.

a.q: A proton NMR spectrum has three peaks with relative areas 3 : 2 : 1. What does the area ratio tell you?
opts: The environments hold hydrogens in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1
The environments have neighbours in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1
The peaks have chemical shifts in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1
The peaks are split into lines in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1
a.why: Peak area is proportional to the number of hydrogens in each environment, so the areas give the ratio of hydrogens, not exact counts. Neighbours and the number of lines come from splitting, not from area.
a.clue: Area under a peak counts something about hydrogens.

b.q: In the spectrum of a compound, one peak is a triplet. How many hydrogens in total are on the carbons next to these hydrogens?
opts: Two
Three
One
Four
b.why: A peak splits into n + 1 lines, so a triplet (3 lines) means n = 2. A student who picks three has counted the lines instead of using n + 1.

problems.detail: A 3 : 2 : 1 area ratio gives only the relative numbers of hydrogens. The right option says the environments 'hold 3, 2 and 1 hydrogens', which reads as exact counts, but 6 : 4 : 2 gives the same ratio. Better wording would be 'hold hydrogens in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1'.
